title: SSO IdP adapter quirks and assertion->audit mapping matrix (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, PingOne)
creator: Asha Menon
description: Objective: Produce a comprehensive IdP-specific compatibility matrix and adapter playbook that documents SAML behaviors, attribute mappings to RBAC v2 entities, audit logging hooks (assertion IDs/session IDs), and per-IdP troubleshooting recipes for Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace (G Suite), and PingOne. Deliverables: 1) Compatibility matrix (supported NameID formats, signing algorithms, ACS binding behaviors, default session timeouts, SCIM provisioning caveats). 2) Adapter playbook with mapping templates for RBAC v2 (role -> group attribute, fallback attribute recipes). 3) Audit integration guidance: how to capture AssertionID, SubjectConfirmation data, and RelayState in our audit logs and link to console events. 4) Onboarding checklist for Solutions/SEs with test cases and expected responses. Scope: - SAML 2.0 SP-to-IdP integration behaviors specific to the four IdPs listed. - Attribute mapping recommendations to map IdP groups/claims to RBAC v2 roles and permissions. - Audit logging schema changes required to include assertion identifiers and correlation IDs. - Sample metadata snippets and verification steps. Out of scope: - Deep SCIM implementation (only call out known provisioning timing caveats). - Non-SAML OAuth/OIDC flows (covered by a separate ticket). Acceptance criteria: - Matrix published in Confluence with per-IdP rows and clear compatibility flags. - Adapter playbook merged to repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sso-adapters PRs linked. - Console shows sample audit events containing assertion_id and nameid for a test tenant. - Onboarding checklist validated by Solutions with at least two customers (one Okta, one Azure) in staging. Test plan highlights: - SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows tested end-to-end. - Clock-skew simulation (+/- 5 minutes) to validate Assertion Conditions handling. - Group membership propagation tests for Google Workspace (delay/SCIM eventual consistency). - Signature algorithm fallbacks (rsa-sha256 vs rsa-sha1) tested against legacy Azure tenants. - RelayState length and character handling tests. Notable recommendations (high level): - Prefer persistent NameID when available; fallback to email (mail/username) with canonicalization. - Always capture AssertionID into audit events and include NameID and InResponseTo fields for forensic linking. - Implement a tolerant audience check that logs but does not silently drop assertions when audience differs by known IdP rewriting patterns (configurable strictness). - For RBAC v2: primary mapping should be via explicit 'roles' SAML attribute (eduPersonScopedAffiliation or custom roles claim); secondary mapping via group membership with normalization rules. - Default session TTL mapping table per IdP (recommendations included).

notes: Per-IdP highlights (summary): Okta: robust SAML metadata; supports persistent NameID and flexible attribute mappings. Known quirks: default RelayState truncation for very long URLs; advise path-based RelayState or session token referencing. Azure AD: excellent metadata availability but older tenants may require rsa-sha1; groupClaims may be filtered (need tenant setting), and SAML session lifetime is often enforced by Azure SSO policies (expect 1h default). Google Workspace: SCIM eventual consistency for group sync and lack of persistent NameID in some configs; recommend mapping using primaryEmail or custom attribute. PingOne/PingFederate: supports multiple ACS endpoints and advanced assertion encryption; common issue is AssertionConsumerServiceIndex mismatch when adapter uses index vs URL - include a fallback to ACS URL matching. Auditing specifics: capture assertion_id (SAML Assertion/@ID), saml_in_response_to (InResponseTo), subject_nameid, authn_instant, issuer, and signature_algorithm in log event. Log both raw (sanitized) assertion reference and interpreted mapping (which RBAC role was assigned). For forensic linking, include correlation_id (generated at SP request creation) and include it in RelayState so it is returned with IdP flow. Migration notes for RBAC v2: when moving from group-based v1 to role-based v2, provide a phased mapping with a 'mirror' mode where both v1 groups and v2 roles are populated for 30 days before cutover.
onboarding_checklist: 1. Verify customer metadata and download IdP metadata XML. 2. Validate NameID format and preferred attribute sets. 3. Confirm signing algorithm; enable rsa-sha256 if possible. 4. Configure RBAC role mappings and test with a non-admin test user. 5. Run end-to-end SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows; capture audit events. 6. If group provisioning used, validate SCIM sync and document expected propagation window. 7. If issues, follow troubleshooting playbook below.
troubleshooting_playbook: Checklist: - Assertion rejected due to audience: log the incoming Audience URI and compare to SP metadata; if mismatch, allow temporary lenient mode and contact IdP admin to adjust allowed audience. - Signature failures: check signing cert rotation; support uploading new cert in metadata and support multiple certs. - Missing groups: check SCIM provisioning logs on IdP side; for Google, expect up to 5 minute delay (documented) and provide manual resync command. - NameID variability: attempt canonicalization (lowercase, strip aliases) and fall back to email attribute. - RelayState lost: prefer using short correlation IDs instead of long URLs; if RelayState empty, correlate via InResponseTo and assertion timestamps. - Assertion replay suspicion: enforce assertion reuse window and maintain short replay cache keyed on assertion_id and issuer. - Audit gaps: ensure assertion_id is included in event pipeline; check Kafka topic for dropped events and backfill if necessary.
testing_notes: Included test cases: TC-01 SP->IdP Okta persistent NameID mapping. TC-02 Azure legacy rsa-sha1 tenant signature acceptance. TC-03 Google Workspace group SCIM eventual consistency. TC-04 PingOne ACS index mismatch fallback. TC-05 Clock skew handling (+/- 5m). Automation: pytest harness + samltoolkit stubs; end-to-end smoke in staging that emits audit events to staging-console, confirm fields via curl to audit API.
